content_units: Uneven Cooling in Your Brisbane Townhouse

A 12-year-old system cooling the lower level to   23°C   while the upper level stays around   28°C   after 2 hours usually points to an   airflow, zoning, duct, refrigerant, or capacity/age-related issue   rather than just dirty filters. In a   145 m² townhouse  , upstairs heat load is naturally higher, but a   5°C gap   is larger than normal and worth diagnosing before spending on major work.
Most Likely Faults and Technician Checks
Issue   Why it fits your symptoms   What the HVAC tech should check   Typical repair direction

Poor upstairs airflow   Cool air often drops downstairs first; weak supply to upper floor leaves it hot   Measure airflow at each supply vent; inspect fan speed; confirm all dampers are open; check return-air path upstairs   Rebalance airflow, adjust fan, open/repair dampers

Leaky, crushed, or disconnected ducts   Common cause of one-floor underperformance, especially in roof spaces   Duct pressure/leak test; visual inspection of flexible duct runs; inspect insulation on ducts   Reconnect, reseal, replace damaged duct sections

Refrigerant undercharge or performance loss   System may still cool somewhat downstairs but struggle to move enough heat overall   Check suction/liquid pressures, superheat/subcooling, coil temperature split, leak signs   Leak repair + refrigerant recharge if justified

Dirty evaporator coil or outdoor condenser issues   Even with clean filters, internal coils can be dirty and reduce capacity   Inspect indoor coil, blower wheel, condensate drain, outdoor coil, compressor amp draw   Deep clean/service coils, fan, drain, electricals

Aging compressor/capacitor/fan motor weakness   Older units can run but lose output, especially in hot Brisbane conditions   Test capacitor values, compressor current, fan motor performance, starting behavior   Replace failed electrical components if cost-effective

Undersized or poorly zoned system   Townhouses often need balancing for upstairs solar/heat gain   Confirm unit capacity against house size/layout; assess zoning and thermostat location   Add zoning/balancing measures or consider replacement

Poor return-air design upstairs   If warm air upstairs cannot return well, cooling there is weak   Check for upstairs return grille, door undercuts, pressure differences with doors closed   Improve return path or transfer air strategy
Service Visit Checklist for Your HVAC Technician
Ask for these checks specifically so the callout stays focused and useful within your   AUD 600 immediate budget  :
-   Airflow test at each vent  , especially upstairs bedrooms and landing
-   Temperature split test   across the indoor coil and at supply/return
-   Inspection of ductwork   for leaks, crushed sections, disconnected branches, and missing insulation
-   Refrigerant pressure/performance test
-   Evaporator and condenser coil inspection/cleanliness
-   Blower fan speed and motor check
-   Capacitor and electrical health test
-   Drainage and ice/frost signs check
-   Thermostat calibration and placement review
-   Return-air adequacy check upstairs  , especially with bedroom doors closed
-   System sizing sanity check   for a 145 m² two-level townhouse in Brisbane conditions
When booking, ask for a   diagnostic-first visit with itemized quote options   rather than authorizing repairs immediately.
Best Repair Path Within 600 AUD
Given your preference to repair first, the smartest near-term approach is:
Option 1: Diagnostic + airflow/duct correction   Best first step for uneven upstairs cooling   Often highest-value fix
Book HVAC
Option 2: Full service with coil/electrical checks   Good if the system has lost overall performance with age   May restore noticeable capacity
Find Service
Option 3: Minor component repair   Sensible only if fault is isolated, like capacitor, fan motor, or damper issue   Usually cost-effective under older systems
Get Quotes
A reasonable   AUD 600 cap   often covers:
- Diagnostic callout
- Basic electrical testing
- Coil/condenser cleaning
- Minor airflow balancing
- Small duct reseal or damper adjustment
- Simple component replacement such as a capacitor
It often   does not   comfortably cover:
- Major refrigerant leak repair plus recharge
- Compressor replacement
- Large duct replacement
- Full zoning retrofit
When Replacement Becomes the Smarter Choice
Replacement is usually the better decision if any of these apply:
- Repair quote is   more than about 30–40% of replacement cost
- The system needs   refrigerant leak repair + recharge   and is already   12 years old
- The   compressor   is failing or replacement is expensive
- Duct/design limits mean the unit will still cool upstairs poorly even after repair
- You have had   multiple breakdowns in the last 2 years
- Energy bills are high and runtime is long with weak comfort results
- The unit uses an   older refrigerant   that is costly or harder to service
For a 12-year-old unit, a   small-to-moderate repair   is reasonable; a   major refrigeration or compressor repair   often is not.
Practical Recommendation for Your Situation
Because your downstairs is cooling but upstairs is not, the   highest-probability causes   are:
-   airflow imbalance
-   duct leakage/damage
-   return-air limitation upstairs
- then   reduced system capacity from age/service issues
With your budget and repair preference, the best move is:
- Spend the first   AUD 200–350   on a   proper diagnostic
- Approve repairs only if they are   airflow/duct/electrical/service related   and keep total spend under   AUD 600
- Start planning replacement instead if the diagnosis shows   compressor weakness, major refrigerant leak, or clear undersizing
